pairs.why: B's key grid sits in rows parallel to the tilted body's edges, while A's body swells unevenly toward the bottom and its keys face the viewer more than the tilted face they sit on.
A's dish hangs on a clear yoke above a flanged base that rests on the sand, while B's tower sinks into the dune and its feed arm runs oddly from the rim to a knob floating above the dish.

A's lifebuoy hangs from a hook on its post and the deck sits on its piles, while B's ring sticks to the edge of the deck at an odd angle and its rope drapes across the planks without a clear attachment.
B is a single coil with a bound loop that sits flat as one object, while A's lasso coil, loose loop and capped ends twist through inconsistent planes and don't read as one continuous rope.
This is the same image pair as p029: B's coiled rope and tied loop hold together, while A's lasso loop and loose capped ends float in inconsistent planes.
A's ring is an ellipse centered on the planet that passes cleanly in front and behind, while B's ring looks off-center and its bands don't line up with the ring's tilt.
B's wheels and side rods run along the rails in one consistent view, while A's red buffer beam and cowcatcher are tilted toward the camera, out of line with the boiler and the track.
The two tables and stools are nearly identical, and both show the board top from slightly higher than the pedestal bases, so neither is clearly built better.
